subject: DPA evidence request: retention, backups, and erase timelines
messages:

Cc: DPO Team <dpo@velorapharma.com>

Subject: Data retention details for DPA review

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our DPO asked for a short write-up and evidence on Redwood's operational controls around retention and deletion for the following items:
- request logs and API access logs (what fields are retained, TTL)
- backup snapshots and the window before deletion
- prompt/input retention for hosted API customers and any ephemeral storage
- procedures for executing customer-initiated data erasure (DPA / GDPR) and typical timelines for full removal from live and backup systems

Could you send the DPA-ready artifact(s) and any diagrams or a short description we can attach to our SCCs review? Preferably by Thursday EOD our time.

Thanks,
Arielle

Hi Arielle —

Appreciate the clear ask. Summarizing what we'll provide:
1) A retention matrix (PDF) that lists per-data-class TTLs and rationale (logs, prompts, embeddings, derived metadata).
2) A backup lifecycle diagram (PNG) showing snapshot cadence, retention windows, and scrubbing procedures.
3) A short narrative describing the steps and average SLA for a customer-initiated erasure request, including restoration/exhumation windows for backups and our approach to cryptographic shredding for keys where applicable.

Two quick notes up front: our hosted API by default stores request metadata (timestamps, request size, model id) and anonymized tracing IDs for 90 days; customer-provided prompts are retained according to the customer's chosen profile — by default 30 days for analytics and cache purposes but can be configured to 0 days for customers on privacy contracts. Backups are incremental daily snapshots with a 30-day hot-window and an additional 60-day cold archive (90 days total) before scheduled deletion; cold archives are encrypted with customer-key options for Private deployments.

Monica and Vivek — looping you in to attach the latest artifacts and confirm technical phrasing.

I'll upload the artifacts and send a single package.

Best,
Grace

Subject: Re: Data retention details for DPA review

Arielle — attaching the two artifacts: 'redwood_retention_matrix_v1.2.pdf' and 'backup_cycle_diagram.png' (see links below). Quick clarifications in-line:

- Request logs: retained for 90 days by default; fields retained are timestamp, model identifier, request latency, error codes, and a hashed request id. We do not store full prompt text in request logs unless the customer uses the default prompt retention setting; where prompt text is retained, we mark it as PII-sensitive and apply stronger access controls.
- Backups: snapshots are incremental; full snapshots are created weekly, daily incrementals are created each night. Hot-window is 30 days; beyond that data transitions to encrypted cold archive for another 60 days before automated deletion. We maintain a manifest that identifies which snapshots contain a customer's data to facilitate targeted deletion.
- Prompt retention: default 30-day retention for model improvement and caching. For customers that require zero retention we offer a contract toggle that disables storage of prompt text and disables upstream model improvement with that customer's data.
- Erasure process: upon validated DPA request we remove live copies within 5 business days. We then schedule deletion from hot backups within the next backup cycle (up to 30 days). For cold archives, we mark manifests for deletion and perform cryptographic key rotation and shredding that renders the archived data unrecoverable; that step can take up to 60 additional days depending on storage provider reclaim cycles.

Evidence links: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/Velora-DPA-evidence (contains PDF + diagram + operational checklist)

Best,
Monica

Thanks Monica — the artifacts look good. A couple of follow-ups from the DPO:
1) For customers that choose the 0-day prompt retention option, does any ephemeral caching still occur in memory/KV caches during inference that could be written to logs?
2) In private on-prem deployments where Velora would manage the keys, can you confirm whether we are required to run any periodic snapshot exports (e.g., for local backups) that would extend retention beyond our configured policy?

If you can confirm by EOD today we'll mark this section as approved for our SCC/contract.

Arielle
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Arielle Berman <arielle.berman@velorapharma.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 16:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention details for DPA review

Hi Arielle — quick answers below. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if you prefer.

1) 0-day retention customers: there is still in-memory KV caching at inference that lives only for the lifetime of the request and is not materialized to persistent logs. We take care that ephemeral caches are not flushed to durable storage; any diagnostic traces are redacted and keyed off hashed request IDs only. So there is no prompt text written to persistent logs in the 0-day profile.

2) Private/on-prem: for Private deployments where Velora manages KMS keys, Redwood does not perform automated snapshot exports out of band. Backup/export behaviour is controlled by the customer's on-prem ops team. We document recommended backup practices in the Private deployment guide, and we can add a contractual clause that Velora will inform Redwood of any manual snapshot exports if you want that in the SCC. By default, there is no additional retention beyond what you configure locally.

If that fits, we'll update the matrix to call out the 0-day profile explicitly and add the private-deploy note.

Regards,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
